{{Quote|There's talk in the Senate about building a palace to house Palpatine, his advisers, and the Imperial Guard.''"<br />"''And statues.|[[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]]|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>}}
The '''Imperial Palace''', originally known as the '''Presidential Palace''' or '''Palace of the Republic''', was a large complex located in the [[Palace District]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], an ancillary of the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]]. Originally built as the official residence for the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the palace also served as an office building, complementing the delegation offices of the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]]. Following the [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|election]] of Chancellor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] was erected to accommodate overflow from the Palace.

Following the catastrophic [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Chancellor Palpatine eradicated the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and declared the reforming of the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and renaming the Palace of the Republic as the Imperial Palace. Expanding the complex significantly, Emperor Palpatine created a labyrinthine maze inside the pyramidal structure and remodeled the palace to serve as the government complex of the Galactic Empire, while the Emperor confined himself to his [[Imperial Throne Room|throne room]] for most of his reign as his primary residence. Following the death of the Emperor and the conclusion of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] the Palace was taken by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and raided, with most functionaries inside being killed in the firefight. After the Palace was secured, the New Republic used it as the residence of the [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] and maintained a large governmental presence in the building. Despite attempts to rename the building the '''Capitol''' or '''Republic House''', or its former title of Presidential Palace, Imperial Palace remained its primary title. 

After surviving several regime changes and millennium of use the palace was severely damaged during [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|the fall of Coruscant]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. While several levels were obliterated during the battle, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] retook Coruscant and the Palace shortly after the end of the war and began the slow process of removing all remnants of the invaders on the uppermost levels of Coruscant's towers. Several decades later the [[Fel Empire|Imperial Remnant]], under the command of Emperor [[Roan Fel]], retook the capital and reoccupied the Palace. Not long after the Imperial conquest, the [[One Sith|reborn Sith]] [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] betrayed the Empire which had aligned with it and deposed Fel. As [[Darth Krayt]] took over the Empire, he used the Palace as his temporary throne as construction finished up on the nearby [[Temple of the Sith]].

==History==
===Galactic Republic===
Constructed by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] on the capital [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the institution's earlier years, the massive complex known as the Presidential Palace was famed across the stars, earning a place on famed historian [[Vicendi]]'s list of the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] in [[10,000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> Serving as the formal residence of the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] for multiple millennia, the Presidential Palace also was a working office for many who served in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="CATCW" /> This tall, brilliant pyramid was located a few bridges away from the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], and could be seen in the distance from the [[Temple district/Legends|Temple district]].<ref name="ATTR">''[[Anakin to the Rescue]]''</ref>

[[File:Prezpalace.png|200px|thumb|The Presidential Palace could be seen from the Temple Precinct]]
During the administration of Supreme Chancellor [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] from [[40 BBY/Legends|40]]-[[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the summit office of the central tower served as his residence; Valorum used the area as a retreat from his busier schedule at the Rotunda's [[Chancellor's working office/Legends|working office]] and often met with advisers and those close to him at the Palace rather than amid the hustle and bustle.<ref name="COD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], the young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was brought to Coruscant by [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]. As he was waiting outside of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to know whether he would be [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] or not, Skywalker grew impatient, and he decided to explore the vicinity of the Temple district. The Presidential Palace caught his [[Eye/Legends|eye]], and after crossing many bridges, the young boy finally reached the brilliant pyramid. He had ventured so far from the Jedi Temple that he could not see it anymore.<ref name="ATTR" />

When [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] ascended to the office of Chancellor, he distanced himself from the Palace and the traditional offices reserved for the Chancellor. Instead Palpatine ordered the construction of the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] to serve as an annex to the Senate Rotunda and to take up overflow from the Palace.<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Instead of residing in the Palace, Palpatine took up an [[Palpatine's apartment/Legends|apartment suite]] in [[500 Republica/Legends|500 Republica]], a stately spire overlooking the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]].<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>

===Galactic Empire===
[[File:ImperialPalaceInterior-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] kneels before [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].]]

Following the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a bloody war orchestrated by Chancellor Palpatine's alter-ego Darth Sidious, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] was disbanded and the Republic reorganized into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Declaring himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], Palpatine removed himself from public affairs and cloistered himself in an [[Imperial throne room (Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center)|audience chamber]] atop the newly christened [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center]].<ref name="DLRODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> Using the facility as a temporary base, the Emperor ordered the refurbishment of the stately governmental palace nearer to the Senate Building, drastically rebuilding the structure until it became the tallest building on the planet.<ref name="UVG">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]''</ref>

In the early days of his reign, Palpatine was nearly killed when [[Gentis]], [[Headmaster/Legends|Headmaster]] of the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]], attempted a [[Ghost Prison incident|military coup]]. The Emperor was [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] via [[Aorth-6]]<ref name="Ghost Prison">[[Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison 2|''Darth Vader and the Ghost Prison'' 2]]</ref> in his [[Imperial throne room (Gentis Coup)|throne room]],<ref name="FC1">[[Dark Times—Fire Carrier 1|''Dark Times—Fire Carrier'' 1]]</ref> and he only survived due to his [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connection]] to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Ghost Prison" /> The finalization of the Imperial Palace was hastened following the attempted coup.<ref name="FC1" />

Taking up residence in the palace, Emperor Palpatine remained isolated at the heart of the massive pyramid, scarcely wandering far and rarely appearing in public. Despite Palpatine's isolationism, the rest of the palace seved as the primary government complex of the Empire, and was constantly with activity, from dignitaries to senators, ambassadors and generals, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] and the mysterious and anonymous [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]]. [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] briefly worked as a preschool attendant at the Imperial Palace for a year, after an incident during the [[Emperor's Ball]] where he mistook the Imperial Supreme Commander Vader for a new model of guard droids.<ref name="DES">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="C-3PO">''[[C-3PO: Tales of the Golden Droid]]''</ref>

In the wake of the death of the Emperor at the climatic [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battle]] over the [[Endor/Legends|Sanctuary Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]] the government officials residing in the Palace were subject to a power vacuum of those vying for the title of Emperor. As [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] declared himself interim Emperor, [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]] began to position herself for ascension to the throne. At the palace, a black veil covered the vacant ceremonial throne during Pestage's rule as to maintain appropriate decorum following the Emperor's death. As Pestage plotted, Isard secretly held Emperor's Hand [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] in the dungeons of the palace and allowed Pestage to feed her information about the mysterious aide to the Emperor.<ref name="Mara">''[[Star Wars: Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand]]''</ref>

[[File:Raid_on_the_Imperial_Palace.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Republic [[Chief of Security/Legends|Chief of Security]] [[Mirith Sinn]] tracks [[Restored Empire|intruders]] inside the Palace during an [[Phase One|Imperial raid]] in [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]].]]

Deciding that Jade was too great a threat to be an ally, Isard ordered the Hand to be brainwashed into giving Isard secrets about the Empire that she was not previously aware of. During the process the Emperor's Hand used a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] to have her interrogator release her and allow her access to a [[computer terminal]]. Isard's men detected this immediately, and she personally began to track Jade through the labyrinthine Palace. Assisted by tech specialist [[Tal Burren]], they eventually realized Jade was in Isard's personal office, but by the time they arrived, she was gone. The Emperor's Hand had stolen one of Isard's datapads with high level security clearance, and was using it to travel through the building unhindered. Jade had left them many false leads, ordering dozens of shuttles to various docking bays; Jade ultimately escaped, something which Isard took personally.<ref name="Mara" />

===New Republic===
As the Empire crumbled, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] thrust forward, openly [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|attacking]] Coruscant and attempting to rout it for good. As the fighting drew to a crescendo, Republic forces shelled<ref name="COTJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> the Palace, one of the last vestiges of the Empire. With the palace's defenses weakened, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] led New Republic troops to the palace, defeating [[General/Legends|General]] [[Tal Ashen]]'s [[Elite Force]] in the process. Marching into the Palace, Skywalker and his troops stormed the entire complex, killing off the last of the remaining [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Guards]] and releasing Imperial-held prisoners-of-war.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref> When the Imperial Palace was secured and the fighting died down, the surviving Imperial officials and functionaries surrendered, and were detained by the New Republic, all of whom were lynched by Republic soldiers, even those who were innocent of any of the Empire's crimes, and also looted various possessions within the palace.<ref name="COTJ" />

[[File:Imperial_Palace_YV_War.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Jedi [[Finn Galfridian]] approaches the New Republic "Imperial" Palace during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].]]

As Coruscant regained a sense of normalcy, the New Republic began to set-up its [[New Republic Senate/Legends|Senate]] and other government agencies on the planet. Using the existing infrastructure, the government took up residence in the Imperial Palace; making significant changes to its exterior, largely to remove damaged structures and repair those areas that were still habitable. The formal residence of the [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]], the Palace served as the primary office building for members of the Senate in addition to offices still kept at the [[Senate Building/Legends|Rotunda]]. Because of the negative connotation associated with the Palace's Imperial name, Republic dignitaries attempted to adopt the title '''Republic House''', even simply calling it '''Capitol'''. Despite many attempts, these efforts fell short and the Imperial title remained.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

Under the administration of Chief [[Borsk Fey'lya]] an extra-galactic race known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] began a [[Yuuzhan Vong War|campaign]] of conquest and destruction across known space. During this time every being about the Imperial Palace was in a constant flutter to process reports of the last world to fall to the invaders. On one occasion young [[Finn Galfridian]], a [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] of Master Skywalker's [[New Jedi Order|reconstructed Jedi Order]], forced his way past the [[Palace Guard (New Republic)|Palace Guards]] and into the Palace in an attempt to warn Chief Fey'lya of an [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] attempt which has been [[Force vision/Legends|foreseen]] by his tutor, [[Dray (Fallen Jedi)|Dray]]. Attacked by the Imperial ambassador, [[Yarmond]], before he could get to the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]], Galfridian was able to deduce that Yarmond was actually the Yuuzhan Vong assassin.<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 1">[[Invasion: Revelations 1|''Invasion: Revelations'' 1]]</ref>

When the Jedi regained consciousness in the confines of a prison cell he was interrogated by Chief Fey'lya despite several attempts to explain himself. Unwilling to believe the Jedi, Fey'lya stormed out of the chamber, unknowingly leaving Galfridian alone to be freed by Dray and his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Prowl]]. Agreeing that Fey'lya, despite his temper and belligerence, needed to be saved, the group split up; while Dray hunted down Yarmond, Galfridian would retrieve his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and other personal belongings.<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 2">[[Invasion: Revelations 2|''Invasion: Revelations'' 2]]</ref> As the Jedi and droid made it to the main levels of the Palace they caused a distraction, only to be captured once more; this time by Guard Captain [[Kopri]]. As Galfridian's droid continued to cause chaos outside the Palace by firing fire bombs, the guards became distracted and the Jedi was able to escape and reclaim his gear.<ref name="Invasion: Revelations 3">[[Invasion: Revelations 3|''Invasion: Revelations'' 3]]</ref>

As the war grew more costly for the Republic and worlds continued to fall, the unthinkable happened. Yuuzhan Vong warships descended on Coruscant, driving the Republic offworld during what history would remember as the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]]. Holed up in the Imperial Palace, Chief Fey'lya drew the onslaught of Yuuzhan Vong warriors up into the heights of the Palace, close enough to the precious data towers that as Chief of State he could not allow fall to the invaders. Surrounded with no way of escape, Fey'lya was executed by Yuuzhan Vong [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Romm Zqar]]; as the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] died, a bomb in tune with his vital signature detonated taking with it 25,000 Yuuzhan Vong warriors, the data towers and most of the Palace's upper levels.<ref name="SBS" />

[[File:Borsk-death.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Chief [[Borsk Fey'lya]]'s [[Kintan strider death gambit|final stand]] in the Palace's highest tower.]]

Before long, [[Shimrra Jamaane]] of the Yuuzhan Vong established his [[Shimrra's Citadel|citadel]] over the ruins of the Palace. Occupying the mobile citadel for only a brief time, the structure was violated by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] during the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar]] and Jamaane was killed. Jamaane's jester and the actual wielder of the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire]], [[Onimi]], drove the Citadel up into the atmosphere, as it was actually a large ship. Despite his attempt to destroy the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who led the attack against the Citadel, Onimi died and the citadel detonated after the Jedi and Alliance soldiers escaped.<ref name="TUF">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>

===Return of the Sith===
Following the Yuuzhan Vong War and the retaking of Coruscant by the Galactic Alliance, the Imperial Palace lay in ruin; toured by members of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] leadership in the immediate aftermath of the battle.<ref name="TUF" /> Despite the damages sustained to the historic structure, the Palace was rebuilt upon the ruins sometime following the stabilization of the government on Coruscant.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Legacy_1_Broken_017.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The Imperial Palace, rebuilt and under the control of the [[Fel Empire]].]]

Reoccupied as of [[130 ABY]], the Imperial Palace was the seat of power for the [[Fel Empire|Galactic Empire]] once more. After the defeat of the Alliance during a [[Sith–Imperial War|costly war]] which saw a joint campaign by the Empire and the [[One Sith|Sith Empire]] under the leadership of [[Darth Krayt]], [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]] took up residence in the Palace and oversaw the functions of the Imperial government. Not long after the conclusion of the war and the surrender of the Alliance, the Sith betrayed Fel and stormed the Palace. Darth Krayt marched into the throne room and assassinated the man seated on the throne, in fact [[Roan Fel's double|one of Fel's doubles]], and declared himself the leader of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|new Sith Empire]]. Krayt ruled with an iron fist from the Imperial Palace; though he quickly moved his base of operations to his newly constructed [[Temple of the Sith]], a massive pyramid erected over the foundations of the conquered [[New Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]].<ref name="L8" />

==Layout==
===Exterior===
[[File:ImperialPalace-RalphMcQuarrie.png|thumb|right|230px|The Palace by day.]]

Located just northeast of the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]] and south of the Jedi Temple district, the Presidential Palace rose from the heart of the [[Palace District]], resembling something like a hybrid of a cathedral and a monumental pyramid. Soaring over all surrounding buildings, the Palace's frame delved deep beneath the scintillating roofs of surrounding structures, finding its roots thrust deep into the planet's bedrock. The Palace was situated at the eastern terminus of the [[Glitannai Esplanade]], a ritzy and famed avenue that ended at the Palace annex known as the ''[[Pliada di am Imperium]]''.<ref name="CATCW" /> Aside from the main building, the palace grounds also had several pyramids made of blue-and-green marble as well as shining gold.<ref name="COTJ" />

Constructed as a government building and a residence for the acting [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the main focal point of the Presidential Palace was that it soared above all surrounding buildings. After the overthrow of the Republic, Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] reconstituted the government as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and renamed the complex as the Imperial Palace. Expanding the complex, the Palace bore much resemblance to a [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]] as construction droids piled on more and more stone. Palpatine's redesigned Palace had a total height of three kilometers, and over two square kilometers in area.<ref name="TNJOS" /> Made up of polished gray-green stone and mirrored crystals, the Palace sparkled in the sun and moon light<ref name="CATCW" />; even at night the Palace never grew dark since blazing illumination from phosphorescent panels, [[glowsphere]]s, and electroluminescence strips kept the structure in a shower of blazing light.

[[File:Imperial_Palace_spires.png|thumb|left|200px|The spires of the Imperial Palace around 3 BBY]]
At least seventy-eight towers<ref name="XWRS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref> erupted from the face of the pyramid, all of them filled with dozens of chambers and rooms serving various functions. Some of these spires were the data towers which housed vital and precious records from across the known galaxy, including survey samples and space charts which could be extremely dangerous to allow to fall into the wrong hands.<ref name="SBS" /> For example, [[Tower 78]] contained at least 443 levels and two hangar bays.<ref name="XWRS" />

Following the war with the Yuuzhan Vong, the Palace was reconstructed upon its old foundations. A central tower supported by thick support structures towered above the cityscape, shirking the stone of its previous incarnation and taking on a modern [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] exterior. Boxy and stepped, the Palace exterior was cris-crossed by many ramps and bridges which kept the building interconnected.<ref name="L8" />

The grounds surrounding the Palace were open to the public and constantly bustling with foot traffic. The [[Palpatine Gardens]], a lush display of finely maintained shrubbery and trees from across the Empire were open to public viewing and could be found in the shadow of the towering pyramid. The Gardens were likewise a stop for tourists undergoing the [[Grand Galactic Tour]], alongside the [[Changing of the Imperial Guard]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game first edition">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref> Aside from these gardens, the Palace also had access to various hanging gardens.<ref name="COTJ" />

===Interior===
====Palace Proper====
The Palace contained over twenty thousand rooms and chambers in fifty connected structures.<ref name="CATCW" /> Numerous architectural styles and design motifs could be found throughout the Palace, changing from one floor to the next. The interior walls of the Palace were made from [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]], and its flooring included [[Wayland marble|marble tiles]] imported from [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]].<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Balance Point">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref> In many of the public areas the structure was open and airy, heavily illuminated via large [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] panes that let in natural light. Other levels deep within the complex were kept dark with carved friezes on the ceiling. As one delved deeper into the sublevels the walls were bare and utilitarian; unadorned floors and chambers were used for military briefings and meetings. At least one part of the palace included a preschool.<ref name="DES" /><ref name="C-3PO" /> Various areas of the palace also had endless and gorgeous mazes of crystal roofs.<ref name="COTJ" />

The [[Grand Corridor]], a towering hallway that wrapped around the entire complex, began at the main entrance of the Palace. Redesigned and expanded by Emperor Palpatine, the chamber was said to have open areas large enough to accommodate a [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]]. The main entrance of the Palace was a massive wall of black stone and red-tinted, cut-glass windows behind which bustled the busy servants of the Empire.<ref name="CATCW" /> Lining the Corridor were rows of exotic [[ch'hala tree]]s which would continuously change color at sound vibrations. Apparently decorative, the trees served a more sinister purpose; the ch'hala's sound-affected bark was a key part of an intricate spy system used by the Emperor and later [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], known as [[Delta Source]].<ref name="HTTE" /> Lining the inner wall of the Corridor's upper tier were several cafes and restaurants whose balconies afforded a clear view of the busy corridor below. Among the many displays of artwork and craftsmanship from across the galaxy was a still-life portrait of the former [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], late-[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Commissioned by Emperor Palpatine himself, the portrait was dedicated to the Emperor's successor and dear friend who lost her life during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|"Jedi Rebellion"]].<ref name="The Last Command 5">[[The Last Command 5|''The Last Command'' 5]]</ref>

[[File:Impalace.png|thumb|right|230px|The Palace by night.]]

Per design, the Grand Corridor allowed access to most of the other public areas of the building. Opulent passageways branched off from the main hall and led to such areas as the [[Imperial Palace Assemblage Auditorium|Assemblage Auditorium]], the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]]' [[Council Chamber (Imperial Palace)|meeting chambers]] and the massive Senate Hall designed after the [[Grand Convocation Chamber]] of the nearby [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Rotunda]]. Accommodating six hundred, six-person [[Repulsorpod/Legends|repulsorpods]] outlined in crimson upholstery, the Senate Chamber was used to hold more private meetings of the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] and later the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]].<ref name="CATCW" /> Additional pavilions, music rooms, and both summer and winter quarters took up other areas of the Palace; a private aviary of [[Hawk-bat/Legends|hawk-bats]] was kept near to the expansive Palace kitchens so that the Emperor and selected guests could have hawk-bat meat or eggs at their leisure. Other areas in the palace included various prisons, treasuries, halls, and various grace-and-flavor residences for concubines, ministers, and trained assassins.<ref name="COTJ" />

On the western face of the central building, the [[Palatial Balcony]] overlooked the [[Glitannai Esplanade]] and the ''[[Pliada di am Imperium]]''. From the balcony, Emperor Palpatine would oversee the parades of the [[Galactic Fair|Imperial Fair]], waving down at his people from on high.<ref name="Star Wars Adventure Journal 5">[[Star Wars Adventure Journal 5|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 5]]</ref> Also adorning the side of the Palace was an information center for tourists. Located on one of the decks that jutted out from the Palace during the time of the New Republic, [[brochure droid]]s and sculptures that had been fitted with speakers were used to allow tourists to access information regarding shuttle departure times, lodgings, eating establishments, and guided tours.

Hangars were situated on multiple levels of the Palace, allowing for emissaries, diplomats, and military personnel to come and go with ease. Access to the Palace airspace was strictly controlled and closely monitored by [[Palace Traffic Control Center|Palace Traffic Control]] which was located in one of the Palace's many towers.<ref name="The Jedi Academy Sourcebook">''[[The Jedi Academy Sourcebook]]''</ref> During the reign of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]], the [[1st Imperial Center Core Defense Squadron]] was housed within a large [[Skull Squadron Hangar|hangar]] near the summit of the central tower.<ref name="Legacy 2006 14">[[Legacy (2006) 14|''Legacy'' (2006) 14]]</ref>

While the Palace was primarily an office building, residential floors existed to house visiting diplomats, ambassadors, late-working staff members, and those members of the galactic regime who remained constantly within the building such as guard and high ranking officials. All of the residential floors of the Palace were accessible from the Grand Corridor and contained extensive libraries<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref> that were open to browsing by guests. The most finely appointed chambers were found on the [[President's Guests floor]], a richly dressed level paneled with hand-carved [[fijisi]] wood.<ref name="CATCW" /> Many famed guests graced the halls of the Imperial Palace throughout its long history. During the New Republic era, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] took up residence in the Palace, in addition to Chief of State [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] and her family.

The [[Imperial Sanctum|Emperor's suite of chambers]] was buried deep within the Palace on floor ninety five and encompassed the working offices of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] alongside a series of hidden Backup Generators for the Coruscant [[Planetary shield/Legends|Planetary Shield]], to be activated automatically in the event of the failure of the main shield.<ref name="Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> During the tenure of Chief Fey'lya as Chief of the New Republic, the Bothan head of state kept his offices in the same area, deep within the Palace core. To give the appearance of being close to the outer wall, Fey'lya ordered the installation of several [[Viewscreen/Legends|holoscreens]] which created the illusion of windows to the outside.

The upper levels of the central tower housed the private offices and residences of the galactic leaders from the construction of the Palace until its destruction. During the time of the Galactic Republic the [[Chancellor's Suite (Presidential Palace)|summit office]] of the tower was a four-sided chamber of reinforced [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] which gave the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] an unobstructed 360 degree view of the cityscape.<ref name="COD" /> This summit tower would last be used by Chancellor [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]], as his successor established the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] to house his [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|primary office]].<ref name="DP" />

[[File:TIEFighterThrone.png|thumb|left|230px|Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] on his throne in the [[Imperial Palace audience chamber/Legends|audience chamber]] of the Palace.]]

After declaring himself Emperor and refurbishing the Palace, Palpatine would meet with members of the Imperial Senate in a large [[Imperial Palace audience chamber/Legends|reception hall]]. A large, sunken auditorium similar in appearance to a crater, the sloping walls of the circular room were lined with layers of audience decks. Each deck had a series of flat stone benches arranged in long arcs, where visitors could come to hear any pronouncements from the Emperor himself. An engineering marvel, the acoustics of the chamber allowed for the Emperor to emit nary a whisper and be heard by all in the chamber as if it were amplified. In turn, the murmurs of the audience could be heard clearly by the Emperor, perched high in the center of the chamber atop a stone pillar which was guarded at its base by six red-robed [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal guardsmen]]. The slanted ceiling of the room was surrounded by gigantic purple and red Imperial banners; an angled, prismatic skylight poured rays of light onto Emperor Palpatine's throne. Several of the pronouncements he often gave often related to the Empire's war against the Rebel Alliance. His main throne room was located at the highest room of the tallest spire of the palace, featuring a transparisteel circular window with a webbed framework behind the throne, and was a long room with curved walls. Various platforms where Red Guardsmen and Stormtroopers were posted were also situated around the throne room. An [[Imperial Palace Awards Auditorium|Awards Auditorium]] was also present at the Imperial Palace, where the Emperor himself would present various medals and honors, including the [[Emperor's Will (medal)/Legends|Emperor's Will medal]], to various Imperial Military personnel for tremendous acts of service to the Emperor.<ref name="TIE">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

When the Palace was rebuilt after the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], a new throne room was built atop its crown. Open-air and spacious, the audience chamber was devoid of furniture save for the throne of the Emperor, which hovered off the marble floor through the employ of a local [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]].<ref name="Legacy 2006 1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref>

====Lower levels====
While the upper levels of the Palace consisted largely of residential floors and government working offices, beneath the structure of the Palace and buried in the bedrock of Coruscant were a series of chambers that held the the lower levels of the Palace, which were a nerve center for the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] and [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]]. Indeed, [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]] kept her office within the Palace, [[Morlish Veed's office|as did]] [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Morlish Veed]] some hundred years later.

There was a blast-shielded war room located in the middle of the second floor that saw heavy use during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and forced may Imperial military personnel to remain at the Palace in event of a major development. Adjacent to the war room was [[the Crypt]], and a computer [[Slicer/Legends|slicing]] and decoding area.<ref name="CATCW" />

The Palace also had a [[Emperor's library|personal library]] where Palpatine conducted his research.

Like other parts of the Palace, the sublevels held many secrets. The [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]], a mysterious group of [[Force Adept]]s trained by Palpatine himself and raised in isolation, ignorant to the existence of other Hands, made use of [[Emperor's Hand training center|training facilities]].<ref name="Mara" /> The Emperor also maintained a hidden [[Palpatine's Spaarti cloning facility|cloning facility]] deep in the Palace where several clone bodies grew in [[Spaarti cloning cylinder]]s.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> The Imperial Palace also included treasuries, including one treasury said to have been built by the legendary "[[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[General/Legends|general]]" [[Toleph-Sor]] and [[Imperial Palace Vaults|hidden vaults]] containing [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] artifacts.<ref name="CATCW" />

===Annexes===
Despite the Palace's already gargantuan size, the Emperor continued to expand the complex until it encompassed fifty different structures. Located along the Glitannai Esplanade was the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Mon Calamari Inglenook|Inglenook]], a wing designed to resemble a coral reef. Enclosed pools within this structure housed protoplasmic [[glurpfish]] and other sea life.<ref name="CATCW" />

Near to the Palace was a [[Ambassadorial habitation pyramid|smaller pyramid]] designed as an exclusive residential complex far closer to the Palace than the older [[500 Republica/Legends|500 Republica]].<ref name="TNJOS" /> Of additional note, Emperor Palpatine's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] maintained a [[Darth Vader's Palace|tower]] nearby, making it his primary residence while on Coruscant.<ref name="SOTE" />

==Palace staff==
Those individuals employed at the Palace were expected to have a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] at all times, because it was so easy to get lost. There were multiple tales of people getting lost in the Palace and never being seen again, and at least one, [[Frona Zeffla]], died at her desk and was not found for at least one standard year.

It was rumored that Palpatine or other high-ranking Imperials covered up unofficial executions as similar disappearances, but those theories were never confirmed. Emperor Palpatine was also said to have encouraged children of workers to play [[Hunter (game)|Hunter]], a hide and seek like game, while their parents were working. Some games were said to have lasted for days.

During the Imperial era, the Palace was guarded by a [[Regiment/Legends|regiment]] of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], as well as the Emperor's Royal Guard and Imperial Intelligence operatives, in a unit known as [[Imperial Palace Guard]]. Because of the enormity of the complex, Palace security was independent of the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] and therefore the head of CSF had no jurisdiction over the Palace. Some of the more secure and private areas were overseen and protected by the mysterious [[Imperial Sentinel]]s.<ref name="SOTESB">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The origins of the Palace, as well that of Coruscant, date back to the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Revenge of the Jedi|Rough Draft]] and Revised Rought Draft of the script for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]; in a scene that was never filmed, the Emperor would have an audience with Darth Vader, with the cityscape of Coruscant would be visible from the throne room.<ref name="secrets">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''</ref> The Imperial Palace was first indirectly mentioned in the [[1978]] novel ''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]'' with a reference to the "Emperor's palace guard",<ref name="Splinter of the Mind's Eye">''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''</ref> and in the [[1979]] comic book [[Star Wars (1977) 27|''Star Wars'' (1977) 27]], in which Princess Leia mentions "the Emperor... skulking in his palace." The Imperial Palace first appeared in the [[1982]] comic book [[Star Wars (1977) 63]].

The Palace was first ever seen in the introduction of the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']] with some of its interior. Around the same time ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' ([[1995]]) provided McQuarrie's concept art and more information about the Palace and its throne room. These sources were used as reference for the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|''Shadows of the Empire'']] project, the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|video game]] and the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|comics series]], drawn by [[Kilian Plunkett]] where the throne room would play a prominent role. The layout of the [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|Tantiss]] [[Throne Room Complex (Wayland)|Throne Room Complex]] was also taken into consideration; [[Jon Knoles]] also suggested to Plunkett the interior architecture of Gothic cathedrals for inspiration.<ref name="secrets" />

[[File:ImpPalaceOtherVersions1.jpg|thumb|right|230px|''Other Versions.'' Various images of the Imperial Palace.]]

The Imperial Palace, or rather, the Presidential Palace, appeared in the [[May]] [[1999]] children's picture book ''[[Anakin to the Rescue]]'', written by [[Cecilia Venn]] and illustrated by [[Chris Trevas]], although it was not specifically identified as such in the story itself outside of it being a "tall, sparkly building." Chris Trevas, in a PM on Facebook to Wookieepedia editor LelalMekha, confirmed that the pyramidal building in question was intended to be the Presidential Palace, citing that he used the late [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s depiction of the Imperial Palace that was first seen in ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]'' as reference, having been sent to him by his publisher.<ref name="Chris Trevas confirmation">"You're right that is the future Imperial Palace. It was specificially mentioned in the book description and the publisher sent me a copy of McQuarrie's artwork as reference. I've been looking for my old files from that job, but I can't seem to find them right now. If I come across the files I will let you know exactly what the book assignment said about the building. Good eye, spotting that building! —Chris" [[Chris Trevas]] PM on Facebook, confirming that the building was intended to be the future Imperial Palace to LelalMekha.</ref>

Some depictions of the Imperial Palace are non-pyramidal in shape, including the palaces shown in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], ''[[Star Wars: Force Commander]]'', ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''. These depictions may either be non-canonical, or simply depict one of the structures in the Palace complex other than the main pyramid. The Imperial Palace's appearance in ''Galactic Battlegrounds'' was reused from the [[Imperial Palace (Monument)|design]] for the "Imperial Palace" monument used frequently by the Empire, including [[Darcc's Palace|one]] owned by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Hindane Darcc/Legends|Darcc]]. The "palace" that appears in ''[[Star Wars: Dark Times]]'' would be the building Palpatine inhabited while the actual palace was under construction, since those scenes take place within a few weeks to a few months after the events in ''Revenge of the Sith.'' In the non-canon ''[[Star Wars Infinities: A New Hope]]'', the Imperial Palace was depicted to be the former Jedi Temple. Ironically, this would later be adopted into the new canon after the Canon/Legends split by Disney.<ref name="Tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref>

It's interesting that some of the latest incarnations of the Imperial Palace seem to depict the non-pyramidal skyscraper like version with a likeness to the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center]] building seen in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Most skyscraper versions seem to occur between Episodes III & IV. This perhaps suggests that later structures were added around the original tower to make it become a pyramid by the time of the events of ''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''.
